title: Medical waste generation and management in medical clinics in South of Iran
author: Dehghani, Ahrami, et al.

steps.title: Select clinics and plan sampling
steps.instruction: Choose 14 medical clinics in the southern region of Iran; schedule random sampling to be performed twice each month for each clinic during weeks with the minimum number of non‑holiday working days, yielding two samples per month, 24 samples per clinic and a total of 336 samples.

steps.title: Collect waste samples at day‑end
steps.instruction: At the end of each working day, visit each selected clinic and collect waste samples from the pre‑segregated containers representing the different waste categories.

steps.title: Label containers and record metadata
steps.instruction: Attach a special label to each waste collection container and record on a form the clinic name, address of the producer, waste type, date of generation, and date of collection.

steps.title: Transport samples to analysis site
steps.instruction: Place the labeled containers in a vehicle and transport them to a suitable location for physical analysis.

steps.title: Weigh samples with PPE
steps.instruction: In a location protected from insects, wear suitable work clothes, mask, tarpaulin gloves, goggles, and forceps; then weigh each waste group separately on a calibrated scale and record each weight in the special form.

steps.title: Record patient count
steps.instruction: For each clinic on the sampling day, record the number of patients who visited the clinic in a separate field of the same form.

steps.title: Calculate per‑capita waste generation
steps.instruction: Divide the total weight of waste collected for the day by the number of patients recorded for that day to obtain the per‑capita waste generation for that clinic.

steps.title: Enter data into SPSS
steps.instruction: Input all recorded weights, patient numbers, and metadata into SPSS software for statistical analysis.

steps.title: Determine mean daily generation
steps.instruction: For each clinic, compute the average daily waste generation for each waste type from the six samples taken from the different waste categories; this yields the mean daily generation per waste type.

steps.title: Estimate annual generation per clinic
steps.instruction: Multiply the mean daily generation of each waste type by 288 (the number of working days per year) to obtain the annual generation per waste type for each clinic.

steps.title: Calculate generalization coefficients
steps.instruction: For each medical specialty, divide the total number of medical units of that specialty in the entire statistical population by the number of sampled clinics of that specialty to obtain a generalization coefficient.

steps.title: Project population‑wide annual waste
steps.instruction: Multiply the mean daily generation (converted to annual by the 288‑day factor) for each waste type by the corresponding generalization coefficient; sum the results across all specialties to obtain the total annual waste generation for the whole population of medical clinics.
